prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your needs (emergency repair vs. planned service, price vs. warranty, location, etc.). That said, here are some Houston companies that consistently get strong local reviews and are worth checking, plus guidance to pick the best one for your situation.

Companies to consider (well-reviewed in Houston)
- John Moore Services — large local company, 24/7 emergency service, long history in Houston.  
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (Houston) — national service network with local crews and emergency availability.  
- One Hour Heating & Air (Houston franchise) — national brand known for on-time service windows and flat-rate pricing.  
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning (Houston) — national company with local technicians and maintenance plans.

How to choose the best one for your repair
1. Verify licensing and certifications
   - Check Texas licensing (TDLR) for air conditioning & refrigeration contractors.  
   - Ensure techs handling refrigerants hold EPA 608 certification.  
2. Read recent reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB) for similar repairs in your area and check how they handle complaints.  
3. Ask about warranties and pricing
   - Get a written estimate or diagnostic fee disclosure.  
   - Confirm labor and parts warranties and whether they honor manufacturer warranties.  
4. Availability and speed
   - If it’s an emergency, confirm 24/7 service and typical response time for your ZIP code.  
5. Transparency and professionalism
   - Ask if they use flat-rate pricing or time-and-materials, whether they provide written receipts, and whether the tech will explain the problem and options.  
6. Get 2–3 quotes for non-emergency repairs or replacements.

Questions to ask a technician when they arrive
- What is the diagnostic fee and is it waived if I authorize the repair?  
- What specifically is broken and what are my repair vs. replacement options?  
- How long will the repair take and do you have the parts on the truck?  
- What warranties come with the repair (labor and parts)?  
- Are there financing or maintenance-plan options?

Red flags
- Vague answers, no written estimate, pressure to agree to expensive replacements immediately, technicians who ask to be paid only in cash and won’t provide a receipt.

If you want, tell me your Houston ZIP code or neighborhood and whether this is an emergency — I can pull up the top-rated companies near you and any current local reviews to help you shortlist 2–3 to call.
